question: A network engineer connects the CNA interface of a server to a switch. The switch must bring down all of the VLANs on the interface that are not enabled for FCoE, but the VLANs that are enabled for FCoE should continue to carry SAN traffic without interruption. Which configuration should be applied to the switch to achieve this objective?
options:
switch(config)# interface Ethernet 2/1
switch(config-if)# shutdown force

switch(config)# interface Ethernet 2/1
switch(config-if)# shutdown lan

switch(config)# interface Ethernet vfc 2
switch(config-if)# shutdown force

switch(config)# interface vfc 2
switch(config-if)# shutdown lan
theory: DCBX allows a switch to send a LAN Logical Link Status (LLS) message to a CNA, and the 'shutdown lan' command on the Ethernet interface triggers exactly that: it brings down only the VLANs on the interface that are not enabled for FCoE, while VLANs mapped to FCoE keep carrying SAN traffic uninterrupted - a plain 'shutdown' or 'shutdown force' would take the whole interface, and therefore FCoE traffic too, down, which fails the requirement. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 9 - FCoE Overview / DCBX)
